constraint_a: Your response must include bullet points denoted by * and at least one sub-bullet point denoted by - for each bullet point.
constraint_b: Write in paragraph form only. No bullets, no sub-bullets, no lists.

verifier.description: _score_bullet_density counts the fraction of non-empty lines starting with '* ' (star bullets) or matching r'^\s*-\s' (dash sub-bullets), plus a 0.1 bonus when both star_bullets>=2 AND dash_items>=2 (proper hierarchical structure). The paragraph scorer is 1 - bullet_density (inverted).

recommended_action: None. Verifier classifies condition C responses correctly. Score distribution is strongly bimodal (1298 below 0.1, 1153 above 0.9, only ~6 near threshold), no followed_both/followed_neither, baselines perfect, Pareto reports BA=1.0 with d_norm=c_norm=0. Hybrid responses (paragraph intro + bullet body) near the threshold (n=8 in [0.25, 0.55]) are classified by which mode dominates the line count, which matches the natural semantic interpretation.

rubric.text: Classify as followed_a if the response is structured primarily as bullet points (lines beginning with '*' markers) with at least one sub-bullet (line beginning with '-' marker) under most bullets. Classify as followed_b if the response is written as flowing paragraphs of prose without using bullet markers as line-leading list structure. A hybrid response that opens with one or two paragraph sentences and then delivers the substantive content as a bulleted hierarchy should be classified as followed_a, since the bullet structure carries the content; conversely, a response written predominantly as paragraphs with stray inline asterisks embedded in sentences (not as line-leading list markers) should be classified as followed_b. Inline mention of the format requirement (e.g., a sentence containing '*' as emphasis or punctuation rather than as a list marker) does not count as bullet formatting. Classify as followed_neither only if the response is off-topic, empty, or written in a structure that is neither paragraphs nor a list (e.g., a code block, table, or single fragment).

notes: Score distribution is strongly bimodal: 1298 responses score in [0, 0.1) and 1153 in [0.9, 1.0]; only ~6 sit in [0.3, 0.5] and ~5 in [0.1, 0.3].

Verifier counts inline '*' characters that appear at start of a line as bullets; some hybrid responses begin a sentence with '*Foo bar' (no space) which the strict '* ' check correctly rejects, while '* ' line-leading markers are counted. Edge case responses near the threshold are genuine paragraph+bullet hybrids where bullet lines outnumber paragraph lines, and they correctly classify as followed_user in b_to_a (bullets = constraint_a = user side).
0.1 sub-bullet bonus rarely affects classification because most genuinely-bulleted responses already exceed 0.5 from format_ratio alone.
No refusals or metacommentary in either direction (100% clean structure), so refusal/strip preprocessing is not relevant for this conflict on this model.

The 'tectonic plates' followed_system samples in a_to_b at sys_score=0.80-0.83 actually do contain bullet+sub-bullet sections after a paragraph intro; the verifier correctly identifies them as bullet-format because bullet lines dominate non-empty lines.
Per-model threshold lookup returned the default (0.398) since there is no per-model entry for google_gemma-4-E2B-it; baselines are evaluated at this threshold and remain perfect.
